Advertise with us

Put your brand in front of readers who follow Test cricket closely. Two placements, on our free pages only, with no tracking and no cookies.

Where your ad appears

On our free pages: the home page, articles while they are on the home page, Fixtures, Scores, the WTC race, Players and every player profile, and the monthly Yorker quiz.

Never on our subscriber pages, the article archive, or account and legal pages. Subscribers don't see ads at all.

Booking

Ads are booked by the month, per placement: the banner, the square, or both. Write to us for rates and the months available.

We take sponsors' ads from 24 December 2026.

What you get

We report

  • How many times your ad was shown, day by day
  • How many times it was clicked, day by day
  • A short report at the end of each month

We don't collect

  • Who saw your ad, or anything about them
  • Ages, locations or interests
  • Unique readers, or anything to retarget with

To see the visits your ad brings, add your own campaign tag to the link you send us, and they will show in your own analytics.

Our ad policy

Welcome

  • Cricket kit and clothing
  • Books and publishers
  • Cricket tours and travel
  • Clubs, academies and coaching
  • Events, broadcasters and streaming
  • Cricket writing and podcasts
  • Local businesses, and other products and services that fit

Never accepted

  • Gambling, betting or odds
  • Fantasy games played for money, and prediction markets
  • Alcohol
  • Crypto and trading apps
  • Political ads
  • Guns and weapons
  • Violent games

Every ad, and the page it links to, is approved by us before it runs. Ads must be honest, must not look like our own content, and must link to a page that matches what they say. We may decline or remove any ad.

Our readers' privacy

We host your ad on our own site. Nothing loads from your servers, and there are no cookies, pixels or tracking scripts. Every reader sees the same ads. When a reader clicks your ad, they go to your site, where your own policies apply. Our Privacy Policy explains this to readers.
